title: Customer Onboard Sprint Retro & Experiment Log
content:
Purpose:
Capture the running list of small, time-boxed adoption experiments we run during the first 90 days of a customer engagement, plus an open retro on what worked/failed. This is intentionally lightweight — use this doc as the single source of truth for the sprint retrospective, experimental hypothesis tracking, and the QBR input checklist for renewal risk signals.

Context / how to use:
- This lives in Drive (working doc).
- Owner assigns experiments with clear success metrics and end dates.
- Capture outcome, lessons, and whether to scale into a standard play.
- Link tickets / call recordings in linked_artifacts and add updates after weekly sync.

Sprint summary (current 30-day window):
- Sprint window: 2025-01-10 -> 2025-02-12
- Customers in scope this sprint: 6 (Mid-market + 2 enterprise pilots)
- Primary adoption metric: daily active MAP features per seat (baseline = 0.6)
- Leading indicator: first meaningful action within 7 days (FMA7)

Baseline metrics (notes):
- Time to first successful API call (hosted): median 24 hours (high variance for enterprise due to IP allowlist)
- Successful sandbox runs / customer: 2.1 in first 14 days
- Support tickets (onboarding category) per customer: 3.2 in first 30 days

Experiment log (format: id | owner | hypothesis | metric | start | end | status | outcome + notes)
1) E-01 | Priya N. | Hypothesis: Shorter pre-configured templates reduce time-to-FMA7 by 40%.
   metric: % customers with FMA7 <= 7 days.
   start: 2025-01-12 | end: 2025-01-26 | status: complete
   outcome: +18% improvement (partial win). Notes: templates helped for PLG customers; enterprise pilots still hit network/setup blockers. Action: add a "network checklist" card to template (owner: Ethan).

2) E-02 | Ben C. | Hypothesis: Dedicated kickoff play (30m engineering pairing) will reduce support tickets by 50% in first 14 days.
   metric: avg onboarding tickets/customer (first 14 days)
   start: 2025-01-15 | end: 2025-02-05 | status: in_review
   outcome (interim): early signal: 35% reduction for customers who took pairing; attendance friction for PLG customers. Action: create optional async video pairing + snippet deck.

3) E-03 | Alicia R. | Hypothesis: Adding a "key success scenario" checklist to the Console reduces time to first meaningful evaluation (TtFME) and improves stickiness.
   metric: TtFME median / adoption rate at 30 days
   start: 2025-01-20 | end: 2025-02-12 | status: running
   notes: early qualitative feedback positive. Need to instrument the Console click-path events. Link: JIRA-CS-4870.

4) E-04 | Ethan M. | Hypothesis: A renewal-risk early-warning card in the onboarding dashboard (flags when MAU < expected and usage is concentrated to 1 engineer) will surface churn earlier and increase renewal outreach success.
   metric: % flagged accounts that convert after outreach within 45 days
   start: 2025-01-25 | end: 2025-02-25 | status: planned
   notes: design mockups ready; need analytics support to build flag logic.

QBR / Renewal input checklist (for CS manager pulling QBR deck)
- Adoption baseline + current sprint delta for core metrics (TtF, FMA7, sandbox runs).
- Active experiments and outcomes with recommended scaling decision (scale / iterate / kill).
- Top 3 product blockers reported by customers this quarter.
- Health signals: login cadence, token spend trend, support volume, feature adoption breadth.
- Renewal cues: contract end date, exec sponsor health, usage trajectory vs committed throughput.
- Ask for QBR: commitment on next-step marketing assets + engineering prioritization if we recommend a concierge rollout for expansion.

30/60/90 adoption plan (experiment-first framing)
- 0-30 days: Diagnose + unblock
  - Goals: First successful end-to-end eval, assign an onboarding owner (SE/CS), run 1 pairing, surface product blockers.
  - Tools: preconfigured templates, network checklist, 30m pairing slot, onboarding Slack channel.
  - Outcomes (success): FMA7 >= 60% of seats & <= 2 support tickets/customer.

- 31-60 days: Iterate + accelerate
  - Goals: Convert early wins to repeatable patterns, increase daily active MAP features, start expansion conversations if usage steady.
  - Experiments: automate in-product tips, measure impact of async pairing video, trial "feature champions" workshop with 1 customer.
  - Outcomes: 20% increase in MAP feature adoption; reduction in time-to-value signals.

- 61-90 days: Solidify + scale
  - Goals: Move customers to self-serve success for common flows, plan renewal engagement for enterprise customers, start ROI story creation.
  - Signals: consistent weekly usage, executive sponsor engaged, at least one success story (quote/data) captured.
  - Outcomes: renewal net retention signaling green / prepare QBR evidence pack.

Retro notes (open, candid):
- What worked: templates reduced back-and-forth for PLG signups; pairing reduced deep-technical confusion for pilots.
- What didn't: "one-size-fits-all" templates fail for networked enterprise customers. Need clearer segmentation.
- Unknowns / follow-ups: exact LTV lift from accelerated onboarding — we can instrument cohort compare but backlog on analytics is a blocker.
- To do: schedule a 45m retro with product ops to prioritize top 2 engineering fixes; update the onboarding template with network card; add a field in the CS playbook for "expected internal owner role" at customer.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Do we have a way to automatically surface customers who tried but never completed the 1st eval? (If not, file ticket.)
- Can growth marketing include 1-2 onboarding tips in the activation email flow? (Priya to confirm.)
- Consider running a small A/B on "pairing before sandbox vs after sandbox" for two cohorts.

Quick links & artifacts:
- Onboard experiments hub (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/Onboard+Experiments+Hub
- Folder: /Drive/customer-success/onboard-assets (designs, videos)
- JIRA quick filters: JIRA-CS-4821 (pairing experiment), JIRA-CS-4870 (console instrumentation)

Next steps (next 14 days):
- Priya: finalize experiment E-02 writeup and add attendance incentives (due 2025-02-16).
- Ethan: scope analytics for E-03 click-path events with infra (due 2025-02-18).
- Alicia: draft QBR evidence pack template and share with Ben for slides (due 2025-02-20).

Notes on tone: Keep this doc as an active log. Drop quick bullets after calls. Avoid over-polish — the goal is speed and clarity for CS + product to act on adoption experiments.

-- end of doc --
